type_of: input protocol and native key decoder repair
name: windows_input_protocol_parity
logic_name: Windows Alacritty keyboard and editing parity

test_list.description: Assert Windows sends balanced CSI-u push/pop and SGR mouse enable/disable bytes through the owned terminal lifecycle.
Map native DEL 0x7f to Backspace so editing removes the preceding grapheme.
Verify VK_BACK and VK_DELETE normalize to distinct Backspace and Delete events.
Treat VK_RETURN LF and otherwise ambiguous C0 LF conservatively as Ctrl+Enter; only VK_J or enhanced CSI-u identifies Ctrl+J.
Retain explicit enhanced Ctrl+J as the legacy newline shortcut.

Preserve CSI-u and bracketed-paste decoding when Windows console character records include paired key-up events; verified RED then GREEN in parity-input-red-release-sequences.txt and parity-input-green-core.txt.

PASS: Windows ConPTY app-level editor test covers ASCII/Unicode editing, middle paste, Ctrl+Enter remaining on one composer row, and Shift+Enter adding the adjacent row. The test moves the cursor to end before checking newline shortcuts; the initial `secondBC` result was correct insertion at document start, so the fixture was corrected rather than weakening behavior assertions. Raw passing output: parity-input-app-editor-final.txt.

PASS: Windows ConPTY child InputReader fixture observed Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Backspace, Delete, and middle bracketed paste while consuming paired native key-up records; raw output is parity-input-green-native-sequence-probe.txt. This verifies the input reader seam, not the polaris-cli composer screen.
Assert every acquired VT reporting mode receives a matching reset on ordinary exit.

inputs.name: Windows native key record
inputs.description: Virtual key, Unicode unit, modifier state and key phase.

inputs.name: terminal writer
inputs.description: VT protocol output stream used to acquire and restore reporting modes.

output_type: normalized KeyEvent plus balanced terminal mode bytes
output_description: Modifier-preserving safe keyboard events, reliable DEL editing and balanced CSI-u/SGR mode lifecycle.
behavior_change: Ambiguous C0 LF and LF tagged as VK_RETURN are treated as Ctrl+Enter (inert in Composer), not Ctrl+J. Ctrl+J remains a newline shortcut only when the J virtual key or enhanced CSI-u Ctrl+J sequence identifies it. This intentionally removes the accidental Ctrl+Enter newline alias.
